ns1:channel.ns1:title: Communications Earth & Environment
ns1:channel.ns1:description:
Communications Earth & Environment is an open access journal from Nature Portfolio that publishes high-quality research, reviews and commentary in the Earth, environmental and planetary sciences. The papers we publish represent significant advances that bring new insight to a specialized area of research. We also provide a community forum for issues of importance to Earth, environmental and planetary scientists, regardless of sub-discipline.

Our scope covers all areas of the geosciences, climate and environmental sciences as well as planetary sciences, including those at the interface with ecology, sustainability and environmental social sciences. Primary research of interest to the journal includes important insights gained from field work, novel analyses of existing data, numerical or analytical modelling, theoretical studies or laboratory experiments.

We encourage submissions that provide independent confirmation of particularly influential publications.

The submission and review processes are managed by our in-house professional editors supported by our Editorial Board Members, who provide technical expertise across the breadth of the Earth, environmental and planetary sciences. We are committed to rapid dissemination of important research results. Articles are published on a continuous basis to ensure swift communication of findings.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Stand-density optimization could substantially increase aboveground biomass in China’s planted forests without land expansion
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 21 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04064-z

Optimizing stand density through targeted planting and thinning could increase aboveground biomass in China’s planted forests by approximately 8.8 Pg without additional land, according to analyses of paired UAV and satellite LiDAR observations, tree density maps, and multiple biomass datasets.
ns1:item.dc:title: Stand-density optimization could substantially increase aboveground biomass in China’s planted forests without land expansion

ns1:item.ns1:title: Evaluation of seismological evidence for decadal changes in Earth’s lowermost mantle and outer core
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 21 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-03961-7

Reported temporal variations in the outer core and lowermost mantle may arise from observational and interpretational artifacts, highlighting the importance of careful validation across independent datasets and thorough testing for potential biases.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Lake- and groundwater-associated alteration of the olivine-rich Margin unit in Jezero crater, Mars
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 21 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-03997-9

Textural, mineralogical, and chemical analyses of the Jezero crater Margin unit from Perseverance’s SuperCam identify multiple episodes of aqueous alteration driven by early carbon-rich fluids, paleolake/groundwater interaction, and late-stage hydrothermal activity.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Spring phytoplankton bloom dynamics reveal thresholds of ocean alkalinity enhancement in the North Sea
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 21 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-03986-y

Ocean alkalinity enhancement displays critical thresholds, beyond which phytoplankton bloom development is delayed and organic matter concentrations are reduced, according to results of mesocosm experiments in the German North Sea.
